body: In this PR I moved the "scripting is disabled" check from ["get the current value of the event handler"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler) to ["the event handler processing algorithm"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-event-handler-processing-algorithm), so that the IDL getters and setters are working even if the scripting is disabled. Oh, you removed the "If scripting is disabled for document, then return null" step, I missed that. You're indeed moving the check, not adding one.

You're right that the IDL setter is just for adding a handler, not invoking it, but it does create a callback that "executes the steps of the event handler processing algorithm" and the _this_ object can be an `OffscreenCanvas`, it seems to me.

I think the reason it previously worked is because of the "If eventHandler's value is an internal raw uncompiled handler" condition, which would only be for Element and Window objects, from `on...` HTML attributes.

What is the expected behavior for normal event handlers registered via `addEventListener()`? I don't see it tested in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/54289 or https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/55479 and I'm not sure what the behavior would be in the spec as it is. If only the "internal raw uncompiled handler" case has a scripting is disabled check, then do other event handlers just fire? This should be possible to test with a click event handler and clicking the element with WebDriver.

The check "Scripting is enabled for an [environment settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#environment-settings-object)" contains of the following checks:
...
* The user has not disabled scripting for settings at this time.
* Either settings's [global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-settings-object-global) is not a [Window](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#window) object, or settings's [global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-settings-object-global)'s [associated Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-window)'s [active sandboxing flag set](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#active-sandboxing-flag-set) does not have its [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag) set.

In the new revision, we want to return the handler to the scripts regardless of the "disabled scripting" state. However we still want to support sandboxed handlers. So de-facto I inlined "scripting is disabled" here and removed the "disabled scripting" check.
